articles.summary: The BBC's Sarah Rainsford reports from the scene of a collapsed residential building in Ukraine's Kyiv region.
articles.body:
At least three bodies have been recovered the site of a residential building that was hit by a Russian strike in the Kyiv region, Ukraine's State Emergency Services said.

A woman in her forties and a teenage boy have so far been identified as rescue workers continue to search the rubble for those who are still trapped.

articles.title: Iran posts video of new underground ‘missile city’
articles.summary: Earlier this week, the Senate narrowly failed to pass a War Powers Resolution that would direct the president to end the war.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — Iran unveiled a launch system capable of firing two missiles at once in a video of its new underground "missile city," Iranian State television reported Saturday.

The video of the double launcher and missile facility comes as tensions rise between the United States and Iran, prompting global concern. Officials from Persian Gulf Countries have called senior U.S. officials in an effort to stop renewed fighting .

Earlier this week, the Senate narrowly failed to pass a War Powers Resolution that would direct the president to end the war.

An oil tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile 11 nautical miles from Oman's Khasab on Saturday, United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said. The tanker was exiting the Strait of Hormuz.

There have been no reported injuries, and the environmental impact is unknown at this time. There have been a total of 148 damaged vessels in the Strait of Hormuz since the U.S. - Iran conflict began, seven of which occurred this week, UKMTO reported.

articles.title: Ataque russo perto de Kiev atinge prédio e deixa mortos e feridos | G1
articles.standfirst: Duas pessoas faleceram e outras quatro seguem hospitalizadas. Prédio de cinco andares, localizado em Dymer, ao norte de Kiev, foi totalmente destruído.
articles.summary: Ataque russo perto de Kiev destrói edifício residencial em Dymer, deixando mortos e feridos, enquanto a Rússia relata alertas de drones em Kaliningrado e no Báltico.
articles.body:
Bombeiros tentam apagar um incêndio após um ataque russo em Dymer, região de Kiev, Ucrânia, domingo, 22 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: AP/Efrem Lukatsky

Um ataque russo atingiu um prédio de apartamentos em uma vila perto da capital da Ucrânia neste domingo (22), matando pelo menos duas pessoas e ferindo outras quatro, de acordo com as autoridades.

O prédio de cinco andares, localizado em Dymer, ao norte de Kiev, foi totalmente destruído.

Equipes de resgate retiraram nove pessoas do pr, incluindo uma criança, enquanto outra foi hospitalizada com ferimentos. Equipes de busca e resgate trabalharam para encontrar outros sobreviventes. O Serviço Estatal de Emergência da Ucrânia informou que acredita-se que 11 pessoas estejam presas nos escombros.

Rússia emitiu um alerta aéreo em Kaliningrado

Em meio ao ataque, um alerta aéreo raro foi acionado em Kaliningrado, um enclave russo próximo à Polônia e à Lituânia, de acordo com o governador local, devido a relatos online de atividade de drones perto de uma importante base naval na região.

O aviso ocorreu horas depois de um ataque com drone no Golfo da Finlândia ter incendiado um navio cargueiro russo com destino à região, que é uma base fundamental para a frota do Báltico da Rússia. Os serviços de emergência finlandeses ainda trabalhavam para extinguir o incêndio no domingo.

Segundo a mídia local, sirenes de ataque aéreo não eram ouvidas em Kaliningrado desde a invasão total da Ucrânia pela Rússia em 24 de fevereiro de 2022.

O governador de Kaliningrado, Alexei Bezprozvannykh, disse que "um objeto suspeito vindo da direção da Lituânia" desencadeou o alerta no distrito de Nemansky, perto da fronteira com a Lituânia, a cerca de 170 quilômetros (105 milhas) a nordeste de Baltiysk.

Em canais russos do Telegram, publicações de usuários que se identificavam como moradores de Baltiysk descreviam o funcionamento das defesas aéreas na região durante a noite.

No domingo, as autoridades de Kaliningrado denunciaram como falsa uma foto, supostamente tirada em Baltiysk, que mostrava nuvens de fumaça subindo ao céu noturno, enquanto uma névoa alaranjada brilhava no horizonte. Elas declararam à mídia estatal russa que a foto “não tinha nada a ver com a região”.

Na manhã de domingo, as autoridades russas não haviam relatado vítimas ou danos em Kaliningrado.

O ministro das Relações Exteriores da Lituânia, Kęstutis Budrys, escreveu no X que a Lituânia "rejeita categoricamente as falsas alegações" sobre o envolvimento do país em um ataque com drones contra a região.

“A República da Lituânia nunca autorizou o uso de seu espaço aéreo para ataques contra alvos na Federação Russa, inclusive no presente caso.”

As autoridades da Lituânia também afirmaram não ter registrado nenhum drone ou objeto similar sobrevoando o espaço aéreo do país na noite anterior.

Equipes de resgate finlandesas combatem incêndio a bordo de navio cargueiro russo

Entretanto, as equipes de emergência tentaram extinguir o incêndio a bordo do navio cargueiro russo Sparta II no Golfo da Finlândia na manhã de domingo, disseram as autoridades finlandesas.

O navio Sparta II derivou para as águas territoriais da Finlândia após o ataque, informou a Guarda Costeira finlandesa. O conteúdo da carga do navio permanece desconhecido.

Um representante da Guarda Costeira disse à emissora finlandesa Yle que a tripulação foi transferida para um navio de resgate russo. Assim que o incêndio for extinto, a embarcação será retirada das águas da Finlândia, afirmou o oficial.

Tanto a Finlândia quanto a Rússia sugeriram que os drones que atingiram o navio eram ucranianos. Até a manhã de domingo, as autoridades ucranianas não haviam se pronunciado.

articles.title: The Drugs Don’t Work
articles.summary: A look at how antibiotic overuse could fuel superbugs, killing eight million people annually by 2050.
articles.body:
The challenges posed by antimicrobial resistance show where its impact is most acutely and tragically manifested: infant mortality in the developing world, specifically in sub-Saharan Africa. This film shows what these bland statistics mean in real terms to the health workers and families affected, following them as they struggle to fight this battle with low-tech solutions.

The Drugs Don’t Work follows the battle to the United Kingdom and examines how and why penicillin, the world’s most successful antibiotic, was invented. It then examines why pharmaceutical companies like GlaxoSmithKline are struggling to produce novel solutions to the problem of antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

The film also explores the cutting edge of academic research at British universities and hospitals supported by the power of the UK-based tech company DeepMind, and features academics and advocates who are devoting their lives to solving the problem. Returning to Africa, it shows how local innovation and the tools offered by the developed world are now saving lives and contributing to the global battle against AMR – an effort that could ultimately save millions of lives.

articles.title: On China, is Trump bucking the US national security establishment?
articles.summary: On China, US is torn between the fears of the national security establishment and the prospect of expanded trade.
articles.body:
On China, US is torn between the fears of the national security establishment and the prospect of expanded trade.

For decades, China was considered the top threat to continued US global primacy, and President Donald Trump’s moves to expand trade with Beijing – even on advanced technology – are rattling Washington’s national security establishment. So when former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argued that the US should sell advanced chips to China to maintain dominance over the AI market, the traditional national security hawks baulked. US political scientist Matthew Kroenig tells host Steve Clemons that “the only one who seems to be unworried is President Trump”.

articles.title: Suspeito de matar manicure foragido; defesa diz ter pedido revogação | G1
articles.standfirst: Advogada afirma que tentava apresentar Celso Miranda de Souza Junior à polícia antes da decretação da prisão preventiva. O g1 não conseguiu confirmar se o pedido foi protocolado na Justiça.
articles.summary: Advogada afirma que tentava apresentar Celso Miranda   à polícia antes da decretação da prisão preventiva. O g1 não conseguiu confirmar se o pedido foi protocolado na Justiça.
articles.body:
Beatriz Borges Monteiro de Castro, de 20 anos, foi encontrada morta com sinais de violência após discutir com seu companheiro em Praia Grande — Foto: Reprodução

A defesa de Celso Miranda de Souza Junior , que está foragido e é suspeito de matar a manicure Beatriz Borges Monteiro , de 20 anos, afirma ter pedido a revogação da prisão preventiva dele. A advogada Luciene Ribeiro de Castilhos alega que estava organizando a apresentação espontânea do investigado à polícia e pede que a prisão seja substituída por medidas cautelares.

Beatriz foi encontrada morta com sinais de violência na casa onde morava com o suspeito, de 27 anos, há cerca de dois meses, no bairro Jardim Princesa, em Praia Grande (SP), na madrugada de sábado (21). O g1 apurou que eles mantinham um relacionamento há cerca de nove meses .

Conforme registrado no boletim de ocorrência, o suspeito deixou o local antes da chegada da equipe policial. Esse foi um dos motivos apontados pela Justiça para decretar a prisão preventiva dele, sob o entendimento de que teria tentado evitar as autoridades.

A defesa, no entanto, afirma que estava organizando a apresentação espontânea de Celso à polícia desde as 11h de sábado (21). Segundo a advogada, a prisão preventiva foi decretada às 13h17, enquanto ela tentava viabilizar o procedimento junto às autoridades.

Por isso, a d efesa contesta a interpretação de que Celso teria fugido para evitar as autoridades e argumenta que a prisão não seria necessária. A advogada também afirma que ele é primário, tem bons antecedentes, residência fixa e trabalha como montador de móveis.

Luciene também alega que o investigado não possui histórico de violência em relacionamentos anteriores . A defesa questiona, ainda, a existência de elementos que comprovem a intenção de matar e contesta o enquadramento do caso como feminicídio qualificado, conforme registrado pela polícia.

A defesa afirma ter pedido que a prisão preventiva seja revogada ou substituída por medidas cautelares. A advogada também diz ter solicitado que a tentativa de apresentação espontânea do investigado à polícia seja formalizada.

O g1 não teve acesso à documentação mencionada pela defesa para comprovar a tentativa de apresentação espontânea nem conseguiu confirmar se ela já foi apresentada à Justiça. Também não foi possível confirmar se o pedido de revogação da prisão preventiva foi protocolado ou analisado pela Justiça.

Entre as medidas sugeridas pela defesa estão o comparecimento periódico à Justiça, a proibição de contato ou aproximação de testemunhas, a restrição para sair da cidade sem autorização e o recolhimento em casa durante a noite e nos dias de folga.

Jovem pediu para dormir na casa da sogra

Antes de ser encontrada morta, . Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, a mulher pensou se tratar apenas de uma discussão comum entre o casal.

Pouco tempo depois, o suspeito também entrou em contato com a mãe. A mulher foi ao local a pedido do filho e encontrou a vítima sem reação no chão da residência. Conforme o boletim de ocorrência, ela acionou o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu).

articles.title: Vestibular UEMS: Redação discute vida saudável e autocuidado em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Milhares de candidatos fizeram as provas neste domingo (22), em Campo Grande e no interior de Mato Grosso do Sul; gabarito preliminar sai na quarta-feira (25).
articles.summary: O vestibular UEMS abordou a saúde dos sul-mato-grossenses na redação; o gabarito preliminar será divulgado nesta quarta-feira (25) pela universidade.
articles.body:
Candidatos chegando para prestar o vestibular da UEMS em Campo Grande. — Foto: Marcus Vinnicius.

O tema da redação do vestibular da Universidade Estadual de Mato Grosso do Sul (UEMS), realizado neste domingo (22), foi: “Existe uma mudança na mentalidade dos sul-mato-grossenses em relação à vida saudável e ao autocuidado?”.

Milhares de candidatos fizeram as provas neste domingo na universidade em Campo Grande e nos câmpus espalhados pelo interior do estado. A universidade ainda não divulgou o número de abstenções do processo seletivo.

O Vestibular UEMS 2027 oferece 1.043 vagas em 52 cursos de graduação, distribuídos em unidades de Campo Grande e municípios do interior de Mato Grosso do Sul.

Na unidade da UEMS na capital, o movimento foi tranquilo pouco antes do fechamento dos portões, às 8h. As provas foram aplicadas até as 13h.

O exame foi aplicado de forma simultânea em 19 municípios: Amambai, Aquidauana, Bataguassu, Campo Grande, Cassilândia, Corumbá, Costa Rica, Coxim, Dourados, Glória de Dourados, Ivinhema, Jardim, Maracaju, Mundo Novo, Naviraí, Nova Andradina, Paranaíba, Ponta Porã e Três Lagoas.

A universidade divulgará o gabarito preliminar das provas objetivas na próxima quarta-feira. Já o resultado final do processo seletivo está previsto para 22 de janeiro.

articles.title: Comerciante levou 12 anos para construir padaria destruída em incêndio | G1
articles.standfirst: Janderson Gadelha, de 35 anos, encontrou imóvel abandonado, alugou o espaço por R$ 500 e começou a trabalhar com a esposa. Fogo destruiu o estabelecimento na sexta-feira (20), em Rio Branco.
articles.summary: Janderson Gadelha, encontrou imóvel abandonado, alugou o espaço por R$ 500 e começou a trabalhar com a esposa. Fogo destruiu o estabelecimento na sexta (20), em Rio Branco.
articles.body:
O incêndio que destruiu uma padaria na Rua Rio Negro, no bairro Conquista , em Rio Branco , na última sexta-feira (20), fez o comerciante Janderson Gadelha, de 35 anos, perder o negócio que construiu ao longo de 12 anos de trabalho.

A padaria era a única fonte de renda da família, formada por cinco pessoas, e também empregava outros cinco trabalhadores.

Ao g1, Janderson contou que trabalhava como motorista e fazia bolinhos em casa à noite, em um pequeno forno na área de casa, para vender e entregar em comércios. Foi com esse dinheiro que conseguiu juntar os primeiros R$ 1 mil para começar o próprio negócio.

Quando encontrou o imóvel onde funcionava uma antiga padaria, mas que estava abandonado, decidiu investir o que havia economizado.

Janderson começou a fazer bolinhos em um pequeno forno na área de casa, à noite, enquanto trabalhava como motorista — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

“A gente alugou por R$ 500 e investiu os mil reais que tinha juntado com a venda dos bolinhos. Comecei a trabalhar lá com minha espoe nossa filha, que tinha 4 anos na época, também ficava com a gente”, contou.

Segundo ele, a rotina era puxada. Além de trabalhar como motorista, Janderson se dedicava à produção dos bolos e às entregas.

Depois que abriu a padaria, continuou trabalhando dia e noite, usando o dinheiro que entrava para comprar matéria-prima, equipamentos e melhorar a estrutura do local.

“Eu ia trabalhando, recebia, comprava matéria-prima de novo. O que ia sobrando, eu comprava tinta, uma telha para tampar uma goteira ou ia comprando maquinário”, relatou.

O comerciante relembra que só descansava apenas quando o corpo já não aguentava mais. Depois de anos de esforço, ele conseguiu estruturar a padaria e se aproximar do que sonhava para o estabelecimento.

Antes do incêndio, Janderson enfrentou outras perdas provocadas por uma alagação, que atingiu a casa e a padaria em 2023 e fez com que ele perdesse praticamente tudo.

Após reconstruir parte do que havia sido afetado, voltou a ter o negócio destruído, desta vez pelo incêndio.

“Não sei qual é o propósito de Deus, mas tenho confiado nele, que não vai me desamparar”, disse.

Com o estabelecimento destruído, ele relatou que precisa de pelo menos R$ 120 mil para voltar a trabalhar . O valor seria usado na compra de equipamentos, matéria-prima e materiais para reconstruir o espaço.

A perda também trouxe preocupação com o sustento da família e dos funcionários, que dependiam da renda do negócio. Sem poder trabalhar, Janderson contou que tem dificuldade para manter as despesas básicas.

“É bem preocupante, porque as coisas não esperam. A fome chega, as contas chegam e a gente sem trabalhar não consegue pagar as contas nem trazer as condições necessárias para dentro de casa. A preocupação também é grande com os colaboradores, porque têm suas necessidades”, relatou.

A família pede ajuda de quem puder contribuir com materiais de construção, mão de obra, maquinário, insumos ou dinheiro. O objetivo é recuperar o estabelecimento e retomar a produção.

Apesar da perda, Janderson diz que espera conseguir recomeçar e reconstruir o que levou anos para conquistar.

“O que eu espero é poder recomeçar, tirar mais um aprendizado dessa história, dar a volta por cima juntamente com todos e voltar a viver uma vida digna”, lamentou.

Teto do estabelecimento desabou e destruiu o maquinário interno que pegou fogo — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros do Acre

O fogo atingiu cerca de 100 metros quadrados do estabelecimento. Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, a equipe foi acionada por vizinhos que perceberam as chamas. O combate durou aproximadamente duas horas e utilizou cerca de 7 mil litros de água.

Parte do teto desabou e o maquinário foi destruído. Entre os itens perdidos estão fatiadores de pão, uma masseira, cerca de 10 armários, uma caixa d'água e aproximadamente 300 bandejas, além de outros materiais usados na produção.

Janderson disse que praticamente nada foi salvo e estima um prejuízo de R$ 300 mil. A única máquina retirada do local foi uma modeladora que estava perto da porta, mas o equipamento era emprestado de um amigo. Ele havia recorrido à máquina porque a própria estava quebrada.

“A única coisa que escapou foi a esperança e a vontade de continuar. Com as coisas materiais foi perda total”, concluiu.

O comerciante ainda não sabe o que provocou o incêndio, mas acredita que pode ter sido um curto-circuito. Ele também não descarta outras possibilidades e as causas ainda serão apuradas.

articles.title: Mumbai wakes up to 16.2°C! Santacruz records the season’s lowest temperature, 5°C below normal, while Colaba stays warmer at 21.8°C. Is sweater weather finally here?
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The city’s minimum temperature dipped to 16.2°C on Saturday, the lowest of the season so far and 5°C below normal at the Santacruz observatory.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The city’s minimum temperature dipped to 16.2°C on Saturday, the lowest of the season so far and 5°C below normal at the Santacruz observatory.However, the city had recorded a lower Nov minimum of 15.7°C last year, on Nov 30. Saturday's reading was also below the 16.5°C recorded on Nov 29, 2024, and 16.3°C on Nov 11, 2016. The lowest Nov minimum on record remains 13.3°C, recorded on Nov 19, 1950.The chill was more pronounced in the suburbs than in south Mumbai. While Santacruz recorded 16.2°C, the Colaba observatory registered a minimum of 21.8°C, 1.7°C above normal.Day temperatures too remained below normal. Colaba recorded a maximum of 32.3°C, 1.5°C below normal, while Santacruz recorded 33.2°C, 0.8°C below normal. Weather enthusiast and independent forecaster Abhijit Modak attributed Saturday's sharp dip to calmer overnight conditions that allowed greater radiational heat loss.He said temperatures had remained relatively higher the previous day because breezy overnight conditions promoted air mixing and prevented significant cooling.In contrast, calmer conditions on Saturday allowed heat to escape more efficiently, resulting in a sharper drop in the minimum temperature. articles.summary: The United States has issued a security alert for its citizens in parts of Mexico's Sinaloa state after armed clashes, road blockades and vehicle fires
articles.body: The United States has issued a security alert for its citizens in parts of Mexico's Sinaloa state after armed clashes, road blockades and vehicle fires were reported following the arrest of suspected cartel figure Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores.In a notice issued on November 21, the US Consulate General in Hermosillo said it was monitoring reports of security operations and unrest in Ahome, Guamúchil, Guasave and Navolato.The consulate urged Americans in the affected areas to shelter in place, avoid non-essential travel and stay away from Mexican Federal Highway 15 between Los Mochis and Culiacan amid the risk of further violence.According to the alert, the clashes, security operations, road blockades and vehicle fires were reported overnight after Meza-Flores's arrest.US citizens were also advised to avoid locations where law enforcement operations were underway and follow instructions issued by local authorities.The consulate asked Americans to remain aware of their surroundings, avoid crowds and monitor local media for updates. It also urged them to keep family members and friends informed about their whereabouts and safety through phone calls, text messages and social media.Travel disruptions warnedThe US mission cautioned that the evolving security situation could disrupt flight schedules and bus services in the region. Americans travelling within or through the affected areas were advised to contact their airlines directly to check flight schedules.Local authorities had also urged residents to remain indoors, restrict movement and avoid Federal Highway 15 between Los Mochis and Culiacan, the alert said.The consulate advised anyone requiring urgent assistance to call 911 in Mexico or contact the nearest US embassy or consulate.It also reminded American citizens that Sinaloa is already classified under Level 4: Do Not Travel in the US State Department's travel advisory for Mexico, the department's highest warning level.The notice provided emergency contact details for Americans seeking assistance. US citizens in Mexico can contact the US Embassy and Consulates at (55) 2579 2000. Those calling from the United States can dial 011 52 55 2579 2000 or +1-301-985-8843.The State Department's Consular Affairs division can also be reached at +1-888-407-4747 or +1-202-501-4444.The consulate urged Americans in the affected areas to monitor official updates and comply with instructions from local authorities as security operations continue.You use AI every day. articles.title: Eddie Vedder's charity has raised over $96 million since 2010 to find a cure for Butterfly Disease; its latest New York gala brought in another $3 million, with Hozier’s surprise performance and support from Tom Holland and Colin Farrell
articles.summary: EB Research Partnership (EBRP), the non-profit co-founded by musician Eddie Vedder and his wife, Jill, raised more than $3 million at its Venture Into
articles.body: EB Research Partnership (EBRP), the non-profit co-founded by musician Eddie Vedder and his wife, Jill, raised more than $3 million at its Venture Into Cures gala in New York on 11 November. The money goes towards research to find a cure for epidermolysis bullosa (EB). EB is a group of rare genetic conditions that cause the skin to be fragile and blister easily. Also known as Butterfly Disease, the condition still has no cure.The gala, held at Pier Sixty, was attended by nearly 700 guests. Irish singer-songwriter Hozier made a surprise appearance and performed three songs. Actor Colin Farrell attended in person, while Tom Holland sent a video message supporting the organisation's mission.“We have reached a remarkable moment in EB. Progress that once seemed impossible is now happening before our eyes,” Michael Hund, CEO of EBRP, said in the organisation's statement. “We have gone from zero FDA-approved treatments to three, while clinical trials have increased 25-fold. Venture Into Cures is more than a celebration of how far we've come; it is a declaration that we are not slowing down. Together, we will keep pushing the boundaries of what is possible until treatments and cures reach every patient and family who needs them.”A surprise on stageComedian Sam Morril opened the evening. The gala reached a crescendo when Eddie Vedder brought out a surprise guest, Irish singer-songwriter Hozier, who performed three songs in support of the charity’s mission to cure EB. Liz Trinnear, a television personality who lives with a milder form of EB, hosted the gala.Tom Holland, who hosted the gala in 2021, couldn’t attend in person this year, so he sent a video message. Academy Award-nominated actor Colin Farrell attended to show his support for the EB community. His documentary, The Slightest Touch, follows his friendship with EB advocate Emma Fogarty. It premieres on 25 November on HBO Max.Honouring John HudsonDuring the event, Faye Dilgen, a board member, paid tribute to her son, John Hudson Dilgen, who lived with EB and died earlier this year. Hudson was one of the EB community's most powerful voices. He reached millions of people and helped inspire more than $720,000 in research support. Dilgen presented the award named in her son's honour to Robbie Twible, who also lives with EB. “John Hudson's greatest wish was that the children who come after him would never know the pain he lived with,” she said.Guests also gave generously during the paddle raise and live auction. Two guitars signed by Eddie Vedder and his Pearl Jam bandmates helped push the total past $1.3 million from those two events alone.Raising money for a causeEBRP works differently from many charities. It takes a financial stake in the research it funds. When a therapy succeeds, the return goes back into new studies. Since 2010, the non-profit says it has raised over $96 million, funded more than 200 projects in 22 countries and grown the number of active EB clinical trials from two to 50.Dr Jean Tang of Stanford University presented an award during the evening and framed the stakes plainly. “Not long ago, families living with EB were told science had nothing to offer them. Today, we have approved treatments and a pipeline full of promise because this community funded the work before anyone else would,” Dr Jean Tang said.The organisation is also testing the same approach on other diseases. Rare Ventures, the non-profit's other initiative, launched with up to $25 million from the Richard King Mellon Foundation and links EBRP with several research institutions, including UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh, Carnegie Mellon University and Stanford Medicine. Its goal is to speed up the development of therapies for rare diseases, which affect more than 400 million people worldwide.Glen McGrath, an executive at Willis Towers Watson who received a leadership award, said he was staying with the cause. “I'm committed to seeing this work through until EB is cured.”Meanwhile, Colin Farrell's documentary will arrive on HBO Max two weeks after the gala, potentially bringing the work to a wider audience.You use AI every day. articles.title: Archaeologists found 70 hair extensions on a 3,300-year-old Egyptian woman; her elaborate hairstyle may have been arranged after death
articles.summary: Archaeologists uncover a 3,300-year-old Egyptian woman adorned with 70 hair extensions, shedding light on ancient grooming practices and hairstyles used after death.
articles.body: Hair extensions may seem like a modern trend today, but they were also widely used thousands of years ago. Nearly 3,300 years ago, an ancient Egyptian woman was laid to rest wearing an intricate hairstyle featuring approximately 70 hair extensions, according to Ahram Online. Rather than being mummified, her body was wrapped in a simple mat. Although researchers in a 2014 study could not determine her name, age, or occupation, she was one of the hundreds of residents who were buried in a cemetery near the ancient city of Amarna whose hair remained intact.Historical context and discovery of Amarna Located on the east bank of the Nile River in modern-day Minya Governorate, Tell el-Amarna was built in the desert as Egypt's new capital during the reign of Pharaoh Akhenaten (circa 1353–1335 BC), only to be abandoned shortly after his death. During excavations at the South Tombs Cemetery, Jolanda Bos, who led the hair research at the South Tombs Cemetery for the Amarna Project, analyzed a selection of 100 excavated skulls and published her findings in the Journal of Egyptian Archaeology.According to the accounts shared by Live Science, Bos’s deep analysis revealed that 28 out of 100 skulls still retained hair, offering rare insight into the grooming practices of the locals. The woman with the most complex coiffure had roughly 70 extensions fastened in multiple layers and heights. While the researcher believed that the woman’s hair was likely styled after death before her burial, she stated that extensions and elaborate styles were also part of everyday life in Amarna.Hair diversity, braids and styling techniques The preserved hair showed considerable diversity among the city’s residents, ranging from very curly black hair to straight brown hair, as well as gray and white. Several skulls with brown hair had either rings or coils around their ears, a hairstyle that was fairly common in Amarna. However, the main reason behind this preference remains unknown.Braids were especially favored in Amarna. As reported by Live Science, Bos observed that the braids were simple three-strand plaits, mostly 1 cm (0.4 inches) wide, with individual strands measuring about 0.5 cm (0.2 inches) when tightly woven. In addition, Bos noted that the residents preferred shorter, shoulder-length styles; standard braids rarely exceeded 20 cm (7.9 inches), while the longest multi-layered extensions reached roughly 30 cm (11.8 inches).Subsequently, Bos shared that a fat-based substance was used to help create all the hairstyles, which inadvertently helped hold the intricate styles in place for millennia after death. At the time, she noted that further research would be needed to determine whether the fat came from animals or plants. Moreover, traces of textile preserved on several of the hair-bearing skulls suggest that residents may have worn fabric coverings over parts of their heads.Covering gray hair naturallyWhile shedding light on one notable case, Bos discovered that a woman had an orange-red color in her gray hair. It may have been dyed with henna, a flowering plant, to hide gray hair. However, Bos and her team of researchers couldn’t confirm what kind of coloring was used on the woman’s hair. Apart from this, they also found dyed hair at other ancient Egyptian sites. This suggests that ancient Egyptians dyed their hair to cover gray strands.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A 61-year-old Pennsylvania supermarket employee bought a scratch-off ticket on her lunch break, and when it lost, she bought another, which won $1 million; she plans to keep working at the store where she bought it
articles.summary: Sometimes, all it takes is one more try for luck to find you. And that's exactly what 61-year-old Andrea Rothwell did.
articles.body: Sometimes, all it takes is one more try for luck to find you. And that's exactly what 61-year-old Andrea Rothwell did. She was on her lunch break when she bought a scratch-off ticket at Tops Friendly Markets in Youngsville, Pennsylvania, where she has worked for five years. Her first scratch-off was a loser, and she turned to leave. But then something told her she had to give it another try. So she went back, and the second ticket she bought won $1 million. It’s no surprise that her co-workers, family, friends and even acquaintances think she has luck on her side. But that’s not the whole story. She did something most people don’t. She gave it a second try. And, well, luck decided to be her pal."So many times, you hear about people winning on the next ticket. I'm glad I went back," she said in a statement to the Pennsylvania Lottery.Despite winning a fortune, Rothwell plans to continue working at the store.A ‘lucky’ lunch breakAndrea Rothwell, 61, from Warren County, works as the dairy and frozen foods manager at Tops Friendly Markets in Youngsville, Pennsylvania. "I was on my lunch break," Rothwell recalls. During her break, she stopped at the machine and decided to buy a ticket. "I actually bought that same ticket twice. The first ticket was a loser. So, I walked away from the machine but then decided to try one more time. That ticket turned out to be the big winner!" She won $1 million from the Million Dollar Win It All ticket, which she bought for $50. That’s not the kind of money she expected to win. So, Rothwell did not trust what she saw at first. She had to ask a co-worker to check the ticket and confirm the number of zeros!She plans to continue workingWinning a million dollars does not mean Rothwell is retiring. She plans to continue working at the store, where she has been employed for five years. So, what is she going to do with her winnings? She plans to invest the money and help her family.Andrea Rothwell’s colleagues are thrilled by her win. "We couldn't be happier for Andrea," Jay Knavel, district manager for Tops Friendly Markets, said in a statement. "Andrea has been part of our Youngsville Tops family for five years, and sharing in her excitement makes this celebration especially meaningful. Her plans to help her family speak to what matters most to her, and our entire team is thrilled to celebrate this incredible moment with her."The Pennsylvania Lottery and Tops Friendly Markets hosted a commemorative cheque presentation on Thursday, 19 November, at the supermarket at 28 Railroad Avenue in Youngsville Borough to celebrate the lucky winner."Celebrating our winners is what it's all about. We are happy that Andrea took a chance on the Lottery during her lunch break and won," Pennsylvania Lottery Executive Director Drew Svitko said. "Our retailers, including Tops Friendly Markets, also play an incredibly important role in serving our players and supporting the Lottery's mission of benefiting older Pennsylvanians."Meanwhile, Tops Friendly Markets will also receive a $5,000 bonus for selling the winning ticket. Scratch-off tickets are distributed at random. The Lottery and its retailers do not know where a winning ticket will be sold until a prize is claimed. Pennsylvania is the only state that directs all its lottery proceeds to programmes for older residents, according to the Lottery. Since ticket sales began in 1972, the state says it has contributed more than $38.2 billion to services such as transport, care services, prescription assistance, senior centres and meals."Our team at the Department of Revenue congratulates Andrea on her $1 million prize, and we wish her all the best as she plans for the future. Her win is a reminder that it only takes one ticket to win a life-changing prize," Secretary of Revenue Pat Browne said. "It's also important to remember that every Pennsylvania Lottery ticket helps support programmes and services for older Pennsylvanians. Since its inception close to 55 years ago, the Pennsylvania Lottery has contributed billions of dollars to programmes that benefit older adults in communities across the Commonwealth."You use AI every day. articles.title: Israeli settlers launch attacks across West Bank as Netanyahu rival decries ‘Jewish terrorism’
articles.summary: Israeli settlers launched a series of attacks across the occupied West Bank, torching at least a dozen cars and vandalizing several homes overnight Sunday, in what Gadi Eisenkot, the main rival of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, decried as “Jewish terrorism.”
articles.body: Israeli settlers launched a series of attacks across the occupied West Bank, torching at least a dozen cars and vandalizing several homes overnight Sunday, in what Gadi Eisenkot, the main rival of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, decried as “Jewish terrorism.” Video from the village of Kufr Malik, about 10 miles northeast of Ramallah, the seat of the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank, showed several cars in flames with thick smoke pouring into the sky as a siren blares in the background. In the same village, a home was tagged with Hebrew graffiti, including the word “revenge.” Similar scenes unfolded in the nearby villages of Deir as-Sudan and Deir Abu Masha’al, two Palestinian communities northwest of Ramallah that were also attacked by settlers. Mustafa Barghouti, the president of the Palestinian National Initiative, said the brazen attacks were part of an escalating pattern of settler violence. “Palestinian families are facing violence, destruction and the loss of their homes,” he said on X. Eisenkot said the violence was the result of the policies of pro-settler, far-right politicians Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, who he said “brought the area to the brink of anarchy.” Smotrich was the key architect of a massive expansion of Israeli settlements and outposts in the West Bank over the last four years, while Ben-Gvir has been accused of turning a blind eye to settler violence. Eisenkot said the attacks were “acts of Jewish terrorism, and we must call them by their name.” Eisenkot, who has four more weeks to attempt to form a government and oust Netanyahu, said the Israeli government should use administrative detention and targeted operations against the assailants. Netanyahu has not issued any public statement about the attacks. CNN has reached out to his office for comment. Netanyahu has repeatedly tried to downplay settler violence, previously saying it was the result of what he has called “juvenile delinquents.” The West Bank has seen a surge in settler violence in recent months, particularly around the annual olive harvest, where Palestinians have repeatedly been harassed and attacked. There have been 410 settler attacks related to the olive harvest since the beginning of September, according to the UN. This weekend’s attacks occurred across several locations in the middle of the night. There were no reports of injuries. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it also received reports of an attack on the Palestinian village of At-Turwani in the southern West Bank near the city of Hebron. The IDF said in a statement it “condemns acts of violence of this nature, which harm public order.” Israeli police said on Sunday they would enter the Palestinian villages under IDF escort to collect evidence. Police have not announced any arrests after the attacks. “Settler terrorism in the West Bank does not take place in a vacuum,” said Yousef Jabareen, the chair of the Arab Joint List party, which saw a surge in support in recent elections. “It is the direct result of the deepening occupation and a government policy under which violence against Palestinians has become an everyday occurrence.” The attacks on Palestinian villages and sites have not been limited to the West Bank. On Thursday morning, a mosque in northern Israel was torched and vandalized with graffiti similar to the messages sprayed across Palestinian homes in the West Bank. Pictures shared by Arab lawmaker Ahmad Tibi showed the inside of the mosque burned and charred. He blamed anti-Arab rhetoric and “people who were poisoned by Netanyahu’s incitement” for the arson. “The police and the Shin Bet must get to the perpetrators. And immediately,” he said on X. Zeena Saifi contributed reporting.

Israeli authorities said November 22, they opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were vandalised and set on fire in four occupied West Bank villages, Deir as-Sudan, Deir Abu Mashaal, Kafr Malik and Al-Tuwani, in attacks a local activist said were carried out by Israeli settlers. Violence in the West Bank, occupied by Israel since 1967, has surged since Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, which triggered the Gaza war.

articles.title: The three amigos
articles.summary: China and Russia are in competition with America and want to harm us. So how do we deal with that?
articles.body:
Michael Corleone is one of the great characters in film history. One of his classic admonitions was to “keep your friends close, but your enemies closer.” It is certainly possible that the most powerful Don, President Trump, had that in mind when meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping last week. Many criticized Trump for playing nice with the two tyrants. The criticism came from both liberal and conservative precincts. How could Trump call Putin his friend? Why isn’t he confronting Xi about stolen technology and other sensitive matters? It is certainly true that China and Russia are in competition with America and want to harm us. So how do we deal with that? Most people have no clue. Incredibly, some members of the Democratic Party want to surrender to Iran, allowing that terror nation to develop nuclear weapons unfettered. Does that sound like a good strategy? And our pal Putin helps Iran’s Mullahs. Outrageous! So how do we deal with the tiny killer? Some isolationist Republicans want to ignore Putin — not our fight, they say. Shall we let Romania handle it? What does Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) want to do about Iran? Or Ukraine? Or Chinese AI development? What’s your plan, Chuck? Former President Barack Obama tried to bribe Iran into behaving, and he had no strategy to stop Putin from killing people. On Obama’s watch, Putin just walked in and subjugated Crimea. Former President Joe Biden surrendered billions of dollars’ worth of weaponry to the Taliban. How did that work out? He had no geo-political strategy at all. And now we have President Trump. Americans need to know that there is no plan B. Military action against China or Russia would lead to mass death. If he is losing an armed conflict, I believe Putin would use nukes, and certainly biological and high-tech weapons would be employed by Russia. Xi is a bit more cautious, but neither of those two tyrants will surrender their vicious goals and tactics. So Plan B is a myth, unless the U.S. is directly attacked. This is why Trump is using deal-making skills like flattery and compromise. The Trump-haters howl with their usual vitriol, but they have nothing other than ineffective economic sanctions to offer. That’s why Trump is calling Putin and Xi his “friends” — replacing Ross and Phoebe, I guess. Trump believes the soft approach is his only option in negotiations with these evil men. He is correct, of course — we cannot attack China and Russia. That is a fairly easy equation. The only thing we can do is develop defensive systems. Trump is hoping his contrived camaraderie will take the edge off, perhaps lessen aggressive behavior from the tyrants. It might not work, but it’s better than any other strategy I’ve heard. Or am I wrong, Chuck? Do you have something better? Bill O’Reilly is an author, podcaster and former cable news host and commentator.

articles.title: Indonesia candy factory fire leaves multiple dead, dozens missing
articles.summary: A massive fire tore through PT Fonusa Agung Mulia's candy factory in Indonesia's Banten, killing at least three with up to 50 workers missing.
articles.body: A massive fire tore through a three-story candy factory in Indonesia's Banten province, killing at least three workers and likely more, and leaving dozens of others unaccounted for as emergency crews fought persistent hotspots into Sunday. Indonesian police removed 24 body bags amid battling the smoldering fire and pausing a search for missing workers overnight, which will resume Monday morning. There were reportedly as many as 300 present for their Saturday shift, but the factory said 24 of the 65 workers involved had returned home, four were receiving medical treatment, 29 remained missing and the whereabouts of another eight had yet to be confirmed. Body bags might contain remains from several people because the intensity of the fire had rendered the recovered victims unidentifiable, police said. The fire broke out at 5 p.m. local time Saturday at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia facility in the Cikande area of the Serang district, which borders the capital, Jakarta. CHINA FIREWORKS FACTORY EXPLOSION: VIDEO CAPTURES DEVASTATING AFTERMATH OF BLAST THAT LEFT AT LEAST 26 DEAD "We have concluded that the victims of this fire cannot be identified through visual inspection," Wahyu Hidayati, a police disaster victim identification official, said. Authorities are collecting DNA samples from relatives and personal belongings of the missing workers. The identification process could take two to three weeks, Hidayati added. WASHINGTON PAPER MILL CHEMICAL TANK IMPLODES, KILLING AT LEAST 1 AND LEAVING 9 MISSING Flames engulfed the structure and sent thick black smoke billowing into the sky, leaving behind twisted metal and blackened, corrugated iron roofing. FIRE ABOARD CARGO SHIP UNDERGOING REPAIRS AT BUSY CHINESE PORT LEAVES 25 PEOPLE DEAD, FIVE MORE INJURED "The figure of 50 refers to those whom we have not yet been able to account for," the factory owner said during a news conference. More than 12 hours after the fire started, 15 fire trucks backed by water cannons were still working to douse hotspots concentrated in the central and rear sections of the building. A joint response team comprising police, military personnel, the Indonesian Red Cross, and volunteers was there, though structural instability made their work difficult. SEATTLE FIRE CREWS RESPOND TO 3-ALARM INDUSTRIAL DISTRICT WAREHOUSE FIRE, ROOF PARTIALLY COLLAPSES "We are conducting sweeps in the areas that have already been brought under control, " Tubagus Mahfud, operations chief of the Serang fire department, said. "Parts of the structure had collapsed, while poor lighting conditions required firefighters to proceed cautiously." Mahfud warned that the factory's production materials posed a high risk of reignition, making thorough cooling operations critical before crews can access the entire building. MASSIVE CHEMICAL FIRE ERUPTS AT ELECTRICAL TRANSFORMER PLANT IN MISSISSIPPI, FORCING EVACUATION "Authorities continue to coordinate with families and the company to determine the whereabouts of employees believed to have been inside the factory when the fire broke out," the Banten Search and Rescue Agency's Rizky Dwianto said. While police said the cause of the fire remains under investigation, survivors told Indonesian media the flames originated from a cooling unit on the third floor. The tragedy adds to a string of deadly industrial fires in Indonesia in recent years that have raised ongoing concerns over workplace safety and emergency preparedness. articles.title: San Francisco braces for massive tides. Mayor urges residents to reconsider travel
articles.summary: Scattered rain continued to exacerbate the impacts of historic flooding across central Florida on Saturday, even as officials in Northern California braced for an unprecedented deluge during high tides heading into the heavy Thanksgiving travel week.
articles.body: Scattered rain continued to exacerbate the impacts of historic flooding across central Florida on Saturday, even as officials in Northern California braced for an unprecedented deluge during high tides heading into the heavy Thanksgiving travel week. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie warned that an “extremely serious” situation was about to hit the city, based on National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and National Weather Service forecasts, and urged people to consider not traveling for the holiday. “We are expecting tides that the National Weather Service told us they have never seen before in recorded history here in San Francisco,” Lurie said via the social platform X. “Take this weekend to get yourself ready, please stock up on supplies, get your shopping done, and know that the city will be out all weekend doing everything possible to protect our residents and our small businesses.” Storm systems impacting Florida and California are an offshoot of El Niño, the natural warming of the Pacific near the equator that warps weather patterns worldwide. Florida typically experiences its dry season from October to May, for example. The expected deluge in California coincides with the highest tides of the year, called king tides. Forecasters said up to 2 feet (0.6 meters) of flooding would be likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways through 6 a.m. Monday, and through 4 p.m. Thursday along other areas of the Pacific coast. Forecasters also warned of dangers Saturday along Florida’s Atlantic coast. The weather service issued marine warnings to boaters tied to thunderstorms capable of creating destabilizing waterspouts, and advised beachgoers to beware of rough surf and dangerous rip currents. NWS meteorologist Melissa Watson in Melbourne said that while the heaviest rains have passed, water levels were expected to continue to rise along the St. Johns River, Florida’s longest, because of continued lighter showers. Near the city of Cocoa, the river rose above a 1953 record Thursday. “Regardless of any additional rainfall, we are expecting these river floods to continue for an extended period of time,” Watson said. Heavy rain earlier this week submerged large swaths of Florida’s Atlantic coast, trapping people in floodwaters in the northeastern part of the state.

articles.title: Paolo Bulgari, jeweler to Princess Diana and Hollywood stars, dies at 89
articles.summary: Italian jeweler Paolo Bulgari, who helped transform his family business into a global luxury house synonymous with Hollywood glamor, has died in Rome at age 89.
articles.body: Italian jeweler Paolo Bulgari, who helped transform his family business into a global luxury house synonymous with Hollywood glamor, has died in Rome at age 89. “The greatest jeweler of our times is gone,” his family said in a statement, according to Italian newspaper Il Sole 24 Ore, remembering him as an “extraordinary figure” who “loved Italy and was an ambassador for Italy all around the world.” The grandson of Bulgari’s founder, he served as chairman of the Bulgari Group from 1984, overseeing the international expansion of the Rome-based jewelry house. In an Instagram post on Saturday, the company remembered him as a “true creative soul” who left “an indelible mark on the world of jewellery” and would continue to inspire future generations. “Everything can be a source of inspiration. There are no rules in creativity. Never,” the jeweler once said, according to the company’s tribute. The cause of his death has not been disclosed. Jeweler to the stars Bulgari became synonymous with Hollywood glamor in the 1950s and 1960s, when stars flocked to its flagship boutique on Rome’s Via Condotti during the city’s La Dolce Vita era. One of its most famous admirers, Elizabeth Taylor, developed a love for the brand while filming “Cleopatra” in Rome, where she began her high-profile romance with co-star Richard Burton, according to Bulgari’s website. Burton gave Taylor a Bulgari emerald-and-diamond brooch for their engagement in 1962, followed by a matching 16-emerald diamond necklace as a wedding gift in 1964, according to Christie’s, which later auctioned both pieces. Burton famously joked that the only Italian word Taylor learned during her time in Rome was “Bulgari,” according to the company. Bulgari’s jewels also became part of one of the most scrutinized royal romances of the 1990s. Diana, Princess of Wales, was also reportedly given a diamond-studded Bulgari ring by Dodi Fayed shortly before the couple died in a Paris car crash in 1997. Other famous admirers included Sophia Loren, Audrey Hepburn, Ingrid Bergman and Grace Kelly. Zendaya, Anne Hathaway and Hudson Williams are among the brand’s modern-day ambassadors. Humble beginnings The company was founded in 1884, when Bulgari’s grandfather, Greek silversmith Sotirios Voulgaris, opened a jewelry shop in Rome after leaving the Ottoman Empire. He later adapted his name as Bulgari in Italian. Born in Rome in 1937, Paolo Bulgari joined the family business in 1960 shortly after leaving school, developing an expertise in precious gemstones. Alongside his brothers, Paolo Bulgari developed its distinctively Italian style, breaking from more delicate jewelry traditions from Paris, by using oversized colored gems, rich yellow gold and bold shapes. The brothers helped expand the company internationally, opening boutiques in New York, Paris and Geneva. The siblings also diversified the company beyond jewelry, moving into watches, perfumes, leather goods and hotels. But the family’s immense wealth also made it a target for kidnappers. In 2005 interview with Italian magazine Panorama, Bulgari recalled personally negotiating the release of his brother Gianni, who was abducted at gunpoint in Rome in 1975 and freed about a month later after a reported 1.3 billion Italian lire ransom payment. Eight years later their cousin and her teenage son were kidnapped from their country estate. Both were released after 35 days, according to a documentary by Italian broadcaster RAI, in which they recounted their kidnapping. In 2011, the Bulgari family sold a controlling stake in the company to French luxury conglomerate LVMH in a deal valued at more than $5 billion, ending more than a century of family control. The funeral will take place on Monday at the Basilica of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme (Basilica of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem), one the seven pilgrims churches of Rome. This story has been updated.

articles.title: What next for Iraq’s push against militias following Jurf al-Sakhar deal?
articles.summary: Baghdad’s deal with Kataib Hezbollah may not end the Iran-backed militia’s influence over the town.
articles.body:
The entry of Iraqi government forces into Jurf al-Sakhar, a town 60km (37 miles) southwest of Baghdad long held by the Iran-backed armed group Kataib Hezbollah, has raised questions about the future of Iraqi militias in the country.

A deal reached between Iraqi authorities and Kataib Hezbollah about control of Jurf al-Sakhar, where oil smuggling was allegedly taking place, staved off a potential confrontation between the two sides.

It is the latest episode in Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s push to assert federal government control over the country and crack down on corruption, which is allegedly funding pro-Iran militias.

So how does Thursday’s compromise bode for the Iraqi state’s mission to rein in militias and weapons outside its control?

Kataib Hezbollah seized Jurf al-Sakhar from ISIL (ISIS) in 2014, renaming it Jurf al-Nasr (“victory”). For the 12 years since then, it has prevented state authorities from re-establishing control and allegedly siphoned oil from local pipelines.

After an intelligence report was released this week about oil smuggling in Jurf al-Sakhar, the government formed a high-level committee to investigate the issue.

After an anti-corruption crackdown was announced, al-Zaidi then gave Kataib Hezbollah until Friday to withdraw from the town. A compromise deal was reached a day before the due date, with government forces entering Jurf al-Sakhar and establishing a joint operations centre in the town. This should see the gradual withdrawal of Kataib Hezbollah units and the phased deployment of an army brigade, a federal police brigade, an energy police regiment and two brigades from the Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF) to the town.

The compromise reportedly came after direct Iranian intervention brokered by Esmail Qaani, head of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) elite Quds Force, which once joined the PMF on the front lines against ISIL and maintains deep ties with several of Iraq’s militias.

PM al-Zaidi, a businessman with a Shia background, took power in May, vowing to end corruption and the fragmentation of the country’s security landscape.

Initially, he set a deadline of September 30 for militias to place their weapons under state control, coinciding with the withdrawal of US and allied forces from Iraq. While US forces withdrew, the militias refused to comply, and the deadline was pushed to June 2027.

Of major concern to Baghdad is the use of Iraq by armed groups to launch unauthorised attacks at Iran’s behest. Since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran, several Iraqi militias have pledged to support Iran’s war effort. Baghdad has acknowledged that attacks targeting neighbours have been launched from its territory and has vowed to put an end to them.

Akeel Abbas, an expert in Iraqi affairs, said Baghdad was the reason for the government’s intervention in Jurf al-Sakhar, not the issue of oil smuggling.

“This area, which the state could not enter since 2014, did actually participate in Iran’s war effort, bombing Gulf countries, bombing US interests in Iraq,” he told Al Jazeera.

“There are other areas, but this one is the strongest, most fortified, and the best weaponry is stored there.”

In July, after Iran-aligned militias attacked Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, the United States and Saudi Arabia launched retaliatory strikes against PMF targets across Iraq, killing at least 20 personnel and drawing condemnation from Baghdad.

By establishing a presence in Jurf al-Sakhr, once the site of former President Saddam Hussein’s military-industrial complex, Baghdad signalled to the US that it was removing it as a potential target.

Zeidon Alkinani, founding director of the Doha-based Arab Perspectives Institute, said the deal over Jurf al-Sakhar was a positive step, especially as it was secured through negotiation and not armed confrontation.

“The remaining questions are how long this will take and what the armed groups will want in return,” he told Al Jazeera. Kataib Hezbollah may also retain its influence in the area through PMF units, with the process of deployment likely to take weeks to complete.

“How the next phases go will determine whether this becomes a real return of state authority or just a rearrangement of who controls the area,” Alkinani said.

Tallha Abdulrazaq, an Iraq expert and strategy and security consultant, said that the deal was compromised by the presence of militia and pro-militia personnel in the security contingent sent by Baghdad.

“Effectively, we’re changing Shia militias for Shia militias, but in uniform,” he said. “There has been no announcement about them being disarmed and their missile and drone manufacturing facilities set up with Iranian expertise being dismantled.”

Iran-backed armed groups have become some of the most powerful actors in Iraq since the US-led invasion of Iraq overthrew President Saddam Hussein’s government in 2003.

Some of Iraq’s most influential militias – like Kataib Hezbollah and Asa’ib Ahl al-Haq – found their genesis in the resistance to US occupation, many with the alleged support of Iran.

Others were formed in response to the threat posed by ISIL after a fatwa was issued by leading Iraqi Shia cleric Ali al-Sistani, fighting under the banner of the PMF.

The PMF are a recognised component of Iraq’s security forces, granting the militias semiofficial status. However, some Iraqi militias, such as Kataib Hezbollah, still operate outside the framework of the state and have been accused of undermining the government’s legitimacy.

There have also been frequent accusations that militias operate corrupt patronage networks to finance themselves, and that their close relationship with Tehran has frustrated the Iraqi government’s efforts to govern the country.

articles.title: Israel’s Eisenkot condemns arson attacks by Jewish settlers in West Bank
articles.summary: Israeli militant settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank early on ​Sunday, starting fires and scrawling racist graffiti, residents said, prompting an accusation of “Jewish terrorism” from the ‌man trying to form an Israeli government.
articles.body: RAMALLAH, West Bank — Israeli militant settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank early on ​Sunday, starting fires and scrawling racist graffiti, residents said, prompting an accusation of “Jewish terrorism” from the ‌man trying to form an Israeli government. The attacks, the latest in an escalation that began after Hamas launched attacks on Israel from the Gaza Strip in 2023, come nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority. Opposition ​leader Gadi Eisenkot has been asked to form a government, though his prospects seem little better. Reuters saw burned-out ​Palestinian vehicles and walls spray-painted with slogans such as “Revenge” in villages near Ramallah. No one immediately ⁠claimed responsibility and no injuries were reported. Eisenkot called the attacks “Jewish terrorism,” saying that “extremist groups that set fire to ​vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel’s national security and ​foreign relations.” He said the policies of Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, ultranationalist ministers in Netanyahu’s Cabinet, had “brought the area to the brink of anarchy, and the authorities have yet to address the crisis.” United Nations bodies and most countries of the world deny ​the legality of the settlements, which make the prospect of an independent Palestinian state ever more remote, a position ​Israel disputes. Israeli police said they had opened an investigation into the attacks, while the military condemned the violence, saying soldiers and police ‌had ⁠been dispatched to the areas of Deir as-Sudan, Deir Abu Masha’al, Kafr Malik and At-Tuwani “following reports and footage showing vehicles being set on fire and graffiti being sprayed in the area.” Ben-Gvir replied in an X post that Eisenkot’s condemnation amounted to selling out to Arab parties, which could be part of a possible new government. Smotrich favors settlement expansion and ​wants Israel to annex the ​West Bank. Yousef Jabareen, head ⁠of the Joint List, the largest Arab party in Israel’s parliament, said the attacks were “the direct result of the deepening occupation and a government policy under which violence against Palestinians has ​become an everyday occurrence,” citing encouragement from Ben-Gvir and Smotrich. Israel’s parliament was sworn in ​on Nov. 10 ⁠without a new government, after the election on Oct. 27 stripped Netanyahu of his majority but left others with no clear path to power. President Isaac Herzog has tasked Eisenkot, who heads the center-right Yashar party, with forming a government, while Netanyahu remains ⁠caretaker prime ​minister. Unless Eisenkot forms a unity government with Netanyahu, he is likely ​to need support from Arab parties to be able to count on a majority of the parliament’s 120 seats. If no one is able to form a ​government, another election will be held next year.

articles.title: Russian cargo ship set ablaze in Baltic Sea drifts into Gulf of Finland
articles.summary: A Russian cargo ship linked to its military was still engulfed in flames Sunday after a suspected Ukrainian drone attack in the Baltic Sea forced its crew to evacuate and sent the damaged vessel drifting into Finnish waters. The 16-member crew aboard the Sparta II escaped in lifeboats following Saturday’s attack and were rescued by…
articles.body:
A Russian cargo ship linked to its military was still engulfed in flames Sunday after a suspected Ukrainian drone attack in the Baltic Sea forced its crew to evacuate and sent the damaged vessel drifting into Finnish waters.

The 16-member crew aboard the Sparta II escaped in lifeboats following Saturday’s attack and were rescued by a nearby Russian ship, according to Finnish Border Guard Commander Ilja Iljin to public broadcaster Yle. The crew was headed back to Russia, while the burning vessel remained anchored in Finland’s waters.

Finnish rescue crews spent the night battling the fire aboard the Russian-flagged cargo ship that was struck while traveling to the Russian exclave Kaliningrad.

Video released by the Finnish coast guard Sunday showed several vessels spraying the ship with water cannons to extinguish the flames and cool containers stacked on its deck.

Finland’s military said Ukraine was likely responsible for the strike, which occurred in international waters west of Russia’s Gogland island in the Gulf of Finland. Ukrainian officials have not publicly claimed responsibility.

The attack prompted Finland to restrict air and maritime traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland, while Swedish fighter jets operating under Finnish command helped patrol the area. Finnish officials also reported a suspected airspace violation by a Russian helicopter during the rescue operation.

Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo warned that the fighting resulting from Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 was reaching dangerously close to his country’s borders.

“War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity,” Orpo wrote Saturday on the social platform X , translated from Finnish to English by the AI tool Grok. “The Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor.”

The Sparta II is owned by Oboronlogistika, a Russian shipping company that provides logistical services to the country’s Defense Ministry. The 397-foot vessel is under U.S. sanctions, though Finnish officials said they had not determined what cargo it was carrying when it was attacked.

articles.title: 'The Social Network' actor Jesse Eisenberg donated a kidney to someone he had never met; after learning that 13 Americans die every day waiting for a transplant, he decided to become a donor
articles.summary: Jesse Eisenberg, the Academy Award–nominated actor, playwright and filmmaker, donated one of his kidneys to a stranger at NYU Langone Health.
articles.body: Jesse Eisenberg, the Academy Award–nominated actor, playwright and filmmaker, donated one of his kidneys to a stranger at NYU Langone Health. Nearly 90,000 Americans are waiting for a kidney transplant, and an average of 13 die every day while waiting. Eisenberg did not know anyone on that list; he simply decided he wanted to help. The act is known as an altruistic, or nondirected, donation. Months after surgery, he has experienced no lifestyle changes, no limitations and no regrets. “I wish I had more kidneys to give,” he says.Why Jesse Eisenberg decided to donate his kidney to a strangerAccording to NYU Langone, the waiting list for a kidney transplant stands at nearly 90,000 Americans, and an average of 13 die every day while waiting. The article states that Eisenberg "didn't know anyone on that list. He simply decided he wanted to help." It describes his donation as "a choice that changes a life" and adds that it is "also safer, and more accessible, than most realise."Nicole M. Ali, MD, a transplant nephrologist at NYU Langone who specialises in living-donor kidney surgery, says, "Receiving a nondirected donor transplant is like winning the lottery." She points to a patient in his 40s who had spent years on dialysis, working night shifts just to accommodate his treatment schedule. After receiving a donor kidney, he came off dialysis almost immediately. "It gives the recipient their life back so quickly," she says.Living kidney donation allows people to donate an organ to strangers in needLiving kidney donation means a healthy person donates one of their kidneys to someone in need. The most common way to donate is a direct donation to someone the donor knows, such as a family member, friend or co-worker. A donor can also give to a stranger through nondirected donation, as Eisenberg did, where a kidney is matched to the best available candidate. In some cases, the article says, the donated kidney becomes the first link in a chain, resulting in multiple transplants.The source states that after donation, the remaining kidney grows to take on the work of two, and the donor goes on to live a completely normal life. According to NYU Langone, more than 7,200 transplants were made possible by living donors in 2025, and kidneys from living donors typically last longer in recipients than those from deceased donors.Medical evaluations determine whether healthy adults are eligible to donate a kidneyEvery donor is screened by a team of doctors, psychologists and former donors, all working to ensure the donor is medically fit and emotionally prepared to donate. Eisenberg says, "Going through all of these medical tests—and coming out with a clean bill of health—only made me more eager to donate." The article states that the evaluation process is open to most healthy adults. Conditions that might prevent donation include uncontrolled high blood pressure, diabetes, significant obesity, certain kidney conditions or a history of some cancers. "Many medical conditions are not necessarily a barrier," says Dr Ali. "Those risks can be carefully assessed and managed."On safety, Dr Ali says, "Living kidney donation is extraordinarily safe." She explains, "We do such a thorough workup that if someone clears the evaluation and is approved to donate, it means they are actually healthier than the general population, with a lower risk of developing kidney disease." As with any surgery requiring general anaesthesia, there are standard risks, but these are carefully assessed during the evaluation. NYU Langone states that for donors who pass the evaluation, long-term health outcomes are excellent, and research shows that donors often outlive their non-donor peers.Kidney donors can typically return to work within two weeks after surgeryThe surgery is typically performed laparoscopically, with small incisions. Most donors spend one or two days in the hospital, with some going home the day of surgery. Donors can typically return to work within two weeks, while those who do heavy lifting are advised to wait four to six weeks to reduce the risk of hernia. A follow-up visit happens around the two-week mark, with continued monitoring after that. The article states that Eisenberg was up and walking the day after surgery, was back on the subway by week two, and by week six was lifting his child and biking through New York City.The one thing that caught Eisenberg off guard was pain in his upper shoulders. "It felt like a muscle ache you'd get after throwing a football around," he says. "That was the extent of my pain." Dr Ali explains that this is a common complaint after laparoscopic surgery: "It's 'referred pain' from air introduced to the abdomen that settles under the diaphragm. It resolves within a couple of days." Eisenberg says, "To me, it was a no-brainer. My sacrifice was a brief hospital stay, a week of discomfort, and five weeks of not picking up my kid." The process begins with a confidential call or email to the Transplant Institute team, followed by a medical and psychosocial evaluation. If cleared, the donor is matched to a recipient and scheduled for surgery.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: How El Chapo Isidro, alleged Mexican cartel leader, was captured
articles.summary: Operation in Sinaloa state resulted in deadly heavy battles between members of security forces and gunmen.
articles.body:
After weeks of careful and detailed planning, Mexican special forces have captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro, a notorious alleged cartel leader on the FBI’s 10 most-wanted list.

Authorities said on Saturday Meza Flores was arrested at a compound in Guasave, in the northwestern state of Sinaloa, following a stealth operation that left four members of the security forces and seven suspected gunmen dead.

The capture highlighted the “unwavering determination to curb organised crime activities to protect and safeguard the public’s peace and security”, the Mexican Secretariat of National Defence said in a statement.

Here’s what we know about how the operation went down:

Meza Flores, 44, is believed to be the leader of the Los Mazatlecos gang, based in Guasave, an agricultural area in Sinaloa.

The group was formerly part of the now-extinct Beltran Leyva Cartel but has operated independently since 2013. Meza Flores had long been subject to arrest in Mexico on charges of organised crime.

He also faces criminal charges in the United States, which had offered a reward of up to $5m for information leading to his capture.

If he is convicted, he could face the death penalty or life in prison.

The operation to capture Meza Flores took place on Friday, but preparations for it began way before.

The Mexican military said the raid, which came after two previous attempts to detain him, was conducted “following coordination” with US intelligence in the “framework of bilateral cooperation”.

Mexico’s Special Forces of the National Guard, the National Army and US intelligence agencies all collaborated on the massive raid operation, according to authorities.

Mexican officials said they had given US intelligence agencies information to locate Meza Flores weeks ahead.

US officials flew reconnaissance drones over the area where he was believed to be holed up, according to The New York Times. Using live video information from the drones, Mexican military analysts were then able to determine the cartel boss’s daily routines.

They also intercepted his communications, including text messages with his mother, wife and sister, to confirm events and meetings he planned to attend, The Times reported.

On Friday, Meza Flores was tracked to a home in Guasave, thanks to phone and radio communications, as well as drone surveillance. Mexican special forces used his voice, build and how he walked to confirm it was him before moving in.

Prior to targeting the home in Guasave, officials first planned two other diversions in Los Mochis, another city in Sinaloa’s northwest.

As the raids distracted cartel members who exchanged fire with the security forces, more than two dozen undercover soldiers from the Joint Special Force elite army unit stormed Meza Flores’s location, The Times reported. They were covered by a ring of dozens of other soldiers, as well as two Mexican Black Hawk helicopters that engaged cartel members positioned in armoured, mounted pick-up trucks in a firefight.

The operation sparked panic across the surrounding area, with gunfire forcing the suspension of a professional baseball game in Guasave, according to local media. Television footage showed players running off the field as loud bangs were heard.

The heavy gun battles between security forces and cartel members left the streets of Guasave smouldering with burned-out cars and destroyed structures.

After the special forces managed to subdue Meza Flores, the tricky issue of exiting Guasave and Sinaloa remained.

That’s where another distraction measure kicked in: two helicopters hovered over the house and then headed in the direction of Los Mochis, creating the impression that Meza Flores was being transported there.

A third stayed back and continued to engage the gunmen.

Amid the chaos, the special forces bundled Meza Flores into an armoured vehicle and drove out of Guasave.

Footage released on social media showed special forces leading a cuffed Meza Flores onto a military transport plane. Early on Saturday morning, the alleged cartel boss arrived in Mexico City, the Mexican defence ministry said in a statement.

In addition to the seven suspected gunmen killed, another eight suspected to be cartel members were arrested, the ministry said, including a man identified as Meza Flores’s cousin and second in command. Another high-ranking member of the gang was identified as the cartel leader’s brother-in-law and the group’s financial operative.

Several weapons and munitions were also seized.
