articles.title: Noah’s Ark search team says wood near Mount Ararat dates to 4,300 years ago, in line with biblical flood
articles.summary: Andrew Jones says lab results date wood from a Noah's Ark site near Mount Ararat to about 4,300 years ago, lining up with the biblical flood.
articles.body: The founder of a team searching for Noah’s Ark in Turkey says initial lab results have dated the wood recovered from the site to approximately 4,300 years ago, a timeline he says lines up with traditional dates for when the biblical flood occurred. "We can announce that the samples date back to about 4,300 years ago, so this lines up with some of the traditional dates for the flood of Noah," Andrew Jones said on "Saturday in America." "So we're in the right time period." Jones said the Noah's Ark Scans team recovered several bags of what he described as "burnt-looking wood." Other pieces of wood collected from the site, located near Mount Ararat, bore markings consistent with tool work. NOAH'S ARK SITE YIELDS FIRST LOOK AT CHARRED WOOD FRAGMENTS RECOVERED DEEP BELOW SOIL The samples were found 30 feet underground on the western side of what Jones called a "boat formation," which he said is about 300 cubits long — matching the size of the ark described in the Bible. AUTHOR DINESH D'SOUZA CHALLENGES BIBLE SKEPTICS WITH 'STARTLING' ARCHAEOLOGICAL DISCOVERIES "What we don't know is how the wood got there. And so we're doing it one step at a time, but we're happy to see this initial results from one of the labs." Jones said he believes he is studying the real Noah's Ark, adding that his team is "following the scientific evidence." "We're checking out every piece of evidence that we gather... and reporting the results wherever the data goes." Jones said interest in the site first began more than 65 years ago when the boat formation was discovered near the place the Bible says Noah's Ark landed. His claims, however, contradict the scientific consensus that the site is merely a natural rock formation. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Despite some opposition to the excavation, Jones said one professor he is working with was impressed by the public interest. "The professor said he was amazed, that he's never been on a project like this where people care so much about archaeology that they want to try to stop us, thinking we're destroying the site," Jones said.

articles.title: Goa getaways to escape the noise and reconnect with yourself
articles.summary: Goa is known for its wild beach parties, crowded shacks and long nights, but the coastal state has another side that is equally worthy of attention.
articles.body: Goa is known for its wild beach parties, crowded shacks and long nights, but the coastal state has another side that is equally worthy of attention. Away from the crowds and well-trodden tourist paths lie places where you can slow down, enjoy your own company and take a much needed break from the everyday routines. Whether it is unwinding at a peaceful beach in the afternoon, savoring a long meal, exploring a hidden café or indulging in a refreshing wellness experience, Goa is full of opportunities to indulge in some undisturbed me-time. Sometimes the best holiday moments are not about cramming in the sights or ticking off attractions, but about doing absolutely nothing and loving every minute of it. If you’re looking to get away from the din, refresh your mind and rediscover the joy of your own company, here are five places in Goa that should be on your itinerary.Renaissance GoaRenaissance Goa is a 175-room hotel in Arpora that offers an experience based on the elements that define Goa – its food and drink culture, Portuguese heritage and coastal influences. Rather than using the destination as a mere backdrop, the property weaves local flavors, design touches and culinary traditions into the guest experience. This philosophy comes to life in a dedicated mixology lab at R Lounge where the team creates fat-washed spirits, tinctures, house-made cordials, infusions, ferments and clarified juices. The cocktail menu draws inspiration from Goan ingredients and food traditions, and features drinks like the Curry 101, prepared with Dukshiri feni, fish-curry syrup, green chili, coriander and lime, and the Azulejo Tonic, a blend of house-made tonic cordial, cucumber and toasted onion seed. At Casa Limone, the culinary experience is Italian with Chef Alessio Cosma Amodio who blends traditional Italian techniques with coastal ingredients. The menu is heavy with handmade pasta, slow-cooked sauces and wood-fired dishes, including squid-ink linguine with lobster, shrimp and calamari, and pizzas with San Marzano tomato sauce. The architectural identity of the hotel is inspired by the visual heritage of Goa, reinterpreted with contemporary design. The entrance is fronted by a sculptural ‘R’ while the lobby is anchored by a custom Navigator Table. The esthetic is carried through the public spaces with mosaic flooring, brass Vanda orchid fixtures, hand-carved sandstone and botanical accents. The design extends to nearly 8,000 square feet of event space, with an LED-lit glass roof that links the interiors to the landscape beyond. Another part of the experience is Renaissance’s global hotel ritual of evenings, a way to mark the transition from day to nite. The Goa property experience is all about Casa Limone, with its lemon tree and cocktails, including a version of Rossini with strawberry purée. The hotel’s mixology, dining, architecture and evening programming combine to give guests ample opportunity to connect with Goa’s distinctive culture and culinary personality.La EstoriaNestled in the heart of Candolim, La Estoria, Goa – IHCL SeleQtions is a boutique retreat that combines Indo-Portuguese heritage with modern comforts, providing guests with a laid-back stay near the coastline. The property is just 700 meters (a 15 minute walk) from Candolim Beach, and close to Goa’s popular beaches and local markets, but still manages to maintain a peaceful, village-inspired atmosphere. The hotel boasts 122 rooms in palm-shaded courtyards, each with a private balcony for guests to soak up the sunshine and the soft evening breeze. The architecture is inspired by the traditional Goan homes with tiled roofs, sunlit verandahs and handcrafted decor to create a sense of place. The rooms and suites have been inspired by Goff, a traditional Goan folk dance, with interiors reflecting themes of community, togetherness and relaxation. If you’re looking for a quick break or a longer holiday, you’ll discover a place that combines local character with modern hospitality. Dining adds another layer to the experience, with Canterbury serving cocktails and Trattoria rustic Italian. The hotel is also ideal for intimate gatherings and private parties, offering elegant indoor rooms and open-air spaces surrounded by tropical greenery. La Estoria is a cozy base for exploring North Goa, with easy links to both Dabolim and Manohar International Airport, an hour away in either direction. With its village-like setting, balcony rooms and proximity to the beach, the property is an attractive choice for travelers seeking a laid-back coastal holiday, where Goan traditions meet modern living.Mansao Curtorim, CGH Earth SahaNestled in the peaceful village of Curtorim in South Goa, Mansao Curtorim by CGH Earth Saha offers an opportunity for travelers to discover Goa beyond its crowded beaches and bustling tourist centers. The villa is a 223-year-old Portuguese heritage mansion that has been restored to its former glory. Blending traditional Indo-Portuguese architecture with modern day comforts, it is a serene retreat amidst lush greenery, historic churches and sprawling paddy fields. The property is about a 30 minute drive to the beaches, and has six elegantly furnished bedrooms, a large living room, a formal dining room, outdoor dining areas and balconies with views of the tropical landscape. Its striking red facade, high wooden ceilings, colonial Goan furniture, rosewood beds and Portuguese-inspired textiles retain the character of its architectural past. At the heart of the mansion lies a stunningly landscaped courtyard, featuring traditional archways and colonial-style galleries, offering an inviting space for relaxation and intimate get-togethers. The culinary experience is a celebration of Goa’s rich and diverse food heritage, with a mix of Portuguese and Indian influences, and menus tailored for vegetarians and meat and seafood lovers alike. Outside the property, guests can explore the quieter side of South Goa with bird watching along the Zuari River, visits to St. Alex Church, nature walks, cycling trails and picnics beside the villa’s private lake. Mansao Curtorim is designed for restorative holidays, creative pursuits and intimate get-togethers, offering a slower, more immersive way to discover Goa’s village life, heritage and natural surroundings.Sol de GoaLocated in Nerul near Candolim, the re-imagined and re-designed Sol de Goa is a blend of Goan heritage, Portuguese-inspired architecture and modern urban elegance to create a contemporary boutique hospitality experience. Celebrated fashion designer Tarun Tahiliani has designed the property and it is a statement in distinctive design esthetics, blending traditional Goan-Portuguese influences with sophisticated interiors and subtle luxury. At the heart of the hotel is a pool courtyard open to the sky, an inviting setting for relaxing afternoons and evenings under the stars. There’s a second swimming pool on the outer deck, which is emerald-hued and surrounded by swaying palm trees. The pool overlooks the surrounding paddy fields, providing a picturesque setting for guests looking for a tranquil retreat. Sol of Goa is designed as a residence style hotel, offering the traveler an intimate and comfortable setting, where one can experience the warmth of home with the amenities of a stylish boutique property. Thoughtfully curated spaces blend relaxed living with elegant design and a vibrant atmosphere, making it ideal for leisurely holidays and memorable getaways. The property’s focus on fine dining also enhances the hospitality experience, providing guests with another reason to stay within its precincts. Sol de Goa is a unique setting to experience the charm of coastal Goa with a blend of heritage inspired architecture, contemporary esthetics, landscaped pool spaces and a personalized ambiance.Thumb Image Courtesy: istockYou use AI every day. articles.summary: Kylie Jenner is making another attempt to sell her sprawling Los Angeles estate, bringing her Holmby Hills mansion back onto the property market with a
articles.body: Kylie Jenner is making another attempt to sell her sprawling Los Angeles estate, bringing her Holmby Hills mansion back onto the property market with a slightly reduced asking price of $38.495 million. The reality television star and beauty entrepreneur has relisted the property for the third time, nearly a year after initially seeking $48 million for it. The latest development was reported by TMZ, while Realtor dot com and The Real Deal have also followed the property’s changing listing history and its substantial price reduction. Jenner purchased the luxury residence in 2020 for $36.5 million. Located in the exclusive Holmby Hills neighbourhood of Los Angeles, the property was initially listed for $48 million in December 2025. However, after several months without a reported sale, the listing was withdrawn before the mansion returned to the market in June 2026 for $38.5 million. The property was subsequently taken off the market again in October, according to Realtor dot com. Its latest appearance on the market, dated November 17, comes with an asking price of $38,495,000, just $5,000 below its previous listing price. The reduction is relatively modest compared with the nearly $10 million cut from its original asking price. At the current asking price, Jenner is seeking approximately $2 million more than she paid for the estate, although the final amount she could receive will depend on negotiations and the eventual sale.Inside Kylie Jenner’s Holmby Hills mansionThe sprawling estate is spread across approximately 15,320 square feet and features seven bedrooms and 14 bathrooms. Designed with privacy and entertainment in mind, the contemporary residence combines expansive living spaces with several luxury amenities. Among its standout features are a basketball court, a fully equipped gym, a geometric zero-edge swimming pool and a private home theatre. The property also includes extensive outdoor spaces and recreational facilities, making it more than just a conventional luxury residence.Its architecture has been described as a modern concrete fortress, with substantial exterior walls and security features that offer residents considerable privacy. The estate’s design and scale were among the highlights of its original marketing when it first entered the market.A changing real estate portfolioThe latest listing comes amid a broader reshuffle of Jenner’s California property holdings. In March 2026, she also put her longtime Hidden Hills residence on the market, initially seeking $20.25 million for the property.That home eventually sold for $15.3 million in September, according to Realtor dot com and property reports. Jenner had purchased the residence in 2016 for approximately $12.05 million, making the sale another significant transaction in her real estate portfolio.She has also been working on a separate, custom-built estate in Hidden Hills. The approximately five-acre property, purchased for a reported $15 million in 2020, has been developed into a sprawling residence with plans for extensive recreational and entertainment facilities. Jenner offered followers a glimpse of the construction and interiors of the new property through a YouTube video in September 2026, showcasing elements of its design and landscaping.Another attempt to find a buyerThe repeated changes to the Holmby Hills listing suggest that finding a buyer at the desired price has not been straightforward. The nearly $10 million reduction from its original valuation represents a significant adjustment, although the property remains among the more expensive celebrity residences currently being marketed in Los Angeles.Matthew and Joshua Altman of Douglas Elliman are handling the latest listing. The brokers did not provide a comment when approached by TMZ about the relisting. For now, Jenner’s Holmby Hills estate remains available to prospective buyers, with its latest asking price placing it just above the amount she originally paid for the property six years ago.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Jim Beam to pause production at flagship Kentucky distillery in major shift for iconic American whiskey brand
articles.summary: Jim Beam shifts bourbon production to its Booker Noe Distillery in Boston, Kentucky, as whiskey inventory hits three times annual U.S. demand, per IWSR.
articles.body: Jim Beam will indefinitely pause production at its historic flagship distillery in Clermont, Kentucky, amid declining whiskey sales and record inventories. The iconic American whiskey brand, owned by Japanese multinational brewing and distilling company Suntory Global Spirits, announced last December that it would pause production at its Clermont, Kentucky facility for one year, with plans to resume operations in 2027, Food Dive reported. However, in a new development, it is now uncertain when the Clermont distillery will begin operations again, the company told The Courier Journal. NEW 123.4-PROOF WHISKEY PROMPTS EXPERT WARNING THAT STRONGER ISN'T ALWAYS BETTER Suntory told the outlet that it manages its Kentucky production in accordance with demand, inventory and long-term needs. The company noted that it plans to reassess production needs in the future. In the meantime, Jim Beam has moved production to its nearby Booker Noe Distillery in Boston, Kentucky, which, with an output of 45 million original proof gallons annually, is the brand’s largest distillery, according to Food Dive. Noe distillery, located on the Clermont facility's campus, will continue its operations producing whiskey labels including Knob Creek, Little Book and Booker's, Inc. reported. Fox News Digital reached out to Jim Beam and the brand’s parent company, Suntory Holdings, for comment. Jim Beam’s move comes amid an ongoing decrease in consumer demand for whiskey, with large quantities of the spirit sitting untouched. Whiskey inventory in the U.S. is three times higher than estimated annual demand, global beverage alcohol data and insight firm IWSR reported in October. "And in most cases, that growth is concentrating at the premium end, while the mainstream and value tiers absorb the pain," he added. articles.title: Meet 16-year-old Anisha Dhoot, student from Oregon, who combined seaweed fertiliser, plastic-waste biochar and AI trained on 17,000 environmental data points to develop a farming tool with 99% accuracy
articles.summary: A 16-year-old student from Oregon has developed an agricultural innovation that brings together seaweed-based fertiliser, recycled plastic waste and
articles.body: A 16-year-old student from Oregon has developed an agricultural innovation that brings together seaweed-based fertiliser, recycled plastic waste and artificial intelligence to address some of farming’s biggest challenges. Anisha Dhoot’s project, called Smart Carbon Recycling, aims to improve damaged soil, support healthier crop growth and help farmers make better decisions about what to plant. Her work combines a low-cost biofertiliser with a machine learning model that analyses environmental conditions and predicts suitable crops, offering a potential solution for farmers dealing with changing climates and declining soil quality.How Anisha Dhoot combined seaweed fertiliser, plastic-waste biochar and AIAccording to the Gloria Barron Prize website, Dhoot developed Smart Carbon Recycling as a way to connect sustainable agriculture with climate action. The project brings together three main elements: seaweed-based fertiliser, biochar made from waste materials and an artificial intelligence system designed to guide crop selection.Her first major development was KelpNutriBoost, a biofertiliser made using kelp collected from the Oregon coast. Dhoot recognised the potential of seaweed as a useful agricultural resource because of its ability to support soil quality and contribute to carbon storage.Kelp grows quickly and can capture carbon from the atmosphere. Dhoot explored how this natural resource could be turned into an affordable product that helps farmers improve soil conditions while supporting more sustainable food production.The project later expanded beyond seaweed. She incorporated carbon-rich biochar produced from recycled plastic waste and sewage treatment plant biosolids. According to the Barron Prize, this combination was designed to improve soil fertility, plant growth rates and the nutritional quality of crops.What makes her EARTH-ai farming tool differentAlongside developing the fertiliser, Dhoot recognised that farmers also needed better information when deciding which crops to grow. Soil conditions and local weather patterns can influence whether a particular crop performs well, making agricultural planning difficult, particularly in areas experiencing environmental changes.She then began developing a machine learning model that could study environmental information and identify crops suited to particular locations.The Barron Prize website states that Dhoot trained her model using a publicly available dataset containing 17,000 environmental parameters. The system analyses local soil and climate conditions to predict which crops are most likely to grow successfully.She named the tool EARTH-ai, which stands for Environmentally Aware Revolutionary Technique for Harvesting.The model reportedly achieves 99% predictive accuracy, making it one of the most notable parts of her agricultural project. It also features a smartphone-friendly interface, allowing farmers to access its recommendations without needing complicated computer systems.Rather than relying entirely on traditional methods or guesswork, the tool aims to give farmers additional information before they decide what to plant.How did a teenager learn to build an AI modelDhoot's achievement also involved learning several technical skills independently. According to the Barron Prize, she taught herself coding through online courses, including a Python programming course led by an MIT professor.She did not begin with all the technical knowledge required to build the system. Instead, she worked towards understanding how programming and machine learning could be used to address an environmental problem.Her work is aimed at helping small-scale farmersAlthough the project involves artificial intelligence and advanced material development, its intended users include small-scale farmers who may not have access to expensive agricultural technologies.The Barron Prize explains that Smart Carbon Recycling is designed to provide farmers, particularly those in developing countries, with a strategy for more climate-friendly agriculture.Soil degradation and food insecurity remain important challenges in many agricultural communities. Deteriorating soil conditions can affect crop productivity, while changing environmental conditions make it harder for farmers to decide which crops are suitable for their land. KelpNutriBoost and biochar are intended to improve soil quality, while EARTH-ai offers information to help farmers select suitable crops.Recognition has helped bring attention to her environmental workDhoot's efforts received national recognition when she was named a 2025 recipient of the Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes.The award recognises young people between the ages of 8 and 18 who have made a significant positive contribution to people or the environment. According to Biochar Today, the prize includes a $10,000 grant to support her initiatives.Beyond developing the technology and fertiliser, she has also worked to bring her ideas into local communities. The Barron Prize reports that she distributes her kelp-based fertiliser to farming communities, organises educational activities and supports fundraising efforts for the Oregon Food Bank.You use AI every day. articles.title: Police: 3 killed and 1 wounded in shooting at Ohio baby shower; 1 man in custody
articles.summary: Three people were killed and one was injured at an Ohio baby shower during an apparent domestic dispute, authorities said.
articles.body: PARMA, Ohio — Three people were killed and one was injured at an Ohio baby shower during an apparent domestic dispute, authorities said. Officers responded to a shooting Saturday evening at Pandora’s Magical Events Venue in Parma, about 10 miles (16 kilometers) south of Cleveland, a police news release said. Authorities said one of the shooters, a 29-year-old man, was taken into custody, but he wasn’t immediately charged. Detectives were trying to determine whether the man was the aggressor or acting in self-defense, police spokesman Scott Traxler said. A second suspected shooter, a 19-year-old man, was one of the people killed, police said. Officials have identified two of the victims as 17-year-old Leasia England and 45-year-old Jayson Townsend. Police said Townsend was the father of the woman for whom the baby shower was being held; she was not injured. Officials haven’t released the names of the 19-year-old suspected shooter who was killed, or a 39-year-old woman who was shot in the leg. Preliminary information indicates that the 19-year-old man was the father of the unborn baby, and witnesses told police that he was not invited to the shower, Traxler said. The man in custody appears to be a relative of the expectant mother. Both firearms involved in the shooting were recovered by police, officials said. Detectives were reviewing surveillance video and witnesses’ statements on Sunday to determine what led to the violent confrontation, Traxler said. Ballistics testing might be required to determine which gun shot each victim. Prosecutors will eventually determine whether the man in custody should be charged with a crime, officials said.

articles.title: Three siblings inherited a Wyoming ranch held by their family since 1928, but a dispute over access and a proposed hospital land sale led to a $101,232 damages award against one sister that the state’s top court upheld
articles.summary: A family property dispute can have consequences beyond disagreements over land access, particularly when a planned development is affected.
articles.body: A family property dispute can have consequences beyond disagreements over land access, particularly when a planned development is affected. In Wyoming, a disagreement between three siblings over a family ranch, a shared access road and a proposed hospital project resulted in a six-figure damages award against one sister. The Wyoming Supreme Court upheld the award after finding that her actions had improperly interfered with a proposed land sale.In a November 20, 2026, decision available on Justia, the Wyoming Supreme Court affirmed the Carbon County District Court's judgment in Davidson v. Schleedlewitz, LLC. The court found that Suellen Davidson had interfered with a business agreement involving her siblings and the Platte Valley Healthcare Project (PVHP), resulting in the cancellation of a proposed property sale.How a family ranch became the centre of a disputeThe case involved Suellen (Sue) Davidson and her siblings, Charles (Chuck) and Deborah (Deb) Davidson. Their family's ranch near Saratoga, Wyoming, had remained in the family since 1928, when their grandparents acquired it.The siblings inherited equal interests in the Davidson Ranch. Their father later conveyed the neighbouring Commercial Property to Chuck and Deb, who owned it in equal shares. Following years of disagreements and litigation, Sue purchased the ranch in 2017 and became its sole owner. She retained an easement allowing her to access the property through a road crossing the neighbouring Commercial Property, which Chuck and Deb owned through business entities. Another road providing access had been blocked by logs since 2019, making the easement road the ranch's only available route.Disagreements developed over Sue's use of the road, including allegations that she interfered with gates and access arrangements. She also complained that her siblings had obstructed the route with fences, vehicles, snow and other barriers.How the proposed hospital sale fell apartIn June 2019, PVHP approached Chuck and Deb about purchasing approximately five acres of the Commercial Property to construct a hospital serving the Saratoga region. The siblings agreed to sell the land for $90,000. They later agreed to include another smaller parcel for an additional $36,000, bringing the total proposed sale price to $126,000.However, the property contained existing easement rights, including Sue's access road. PVHP therefore began discussions with the siblings and other interested parties to relocate the road and address access arrangements. Sue learned about the proposed hospital project in November 2019. In January 2020, she recorded a notice of lis pendens against the Commercial Property in connection with separate litigation involving her siblings. Such a notice alerts potential buyers and other parties that a property is subject to ongoing legal proceedings.PVHP subsequently discovered the notice during a title search and became concerned that it could prevent the sellers from providing clear title. The healthcare project asked Chuck and Deb to resolve the issue within 30 days. Meanwhile, PVHP offered Sue $10,000 for her easement rights and proposed alternative access to the ranch. Sue responded with additional demands, including construction of a new gravel road and other improvements.PVHP never responded to her counteroffer. On April 20, 2020, PVHP informed Chuck that it was abandoning the deal because of concerns about delays caused by the lis pendens and the related litigation. It eventually found another property for the hospital.Why the Wyoming Supreme Court upheld the $101,232 awardChuck and Deb subsequently sued Sue for intentional interference with a business expectancy. After a five-day trial, the Carbon County District Court ruled against her, finding that her actions had contributed to the failed hospital sale. It ordered her to pay $101,232 in damages and also required her to pay for relocating the easement road. Sue appealed, arguing that filing the lis pendens was protected by litigation privilege and that the damages award was excessive.The Wyoming Supreme Court rejected her arguments. It held that filing a lis pendens is not absolutely protected from liability for intentional interference with a business expectancy. Instead, a qualified privilege applies when someone acts in good faith to protect a legally recognised interest through appropriate means. The court found that Sue's conduct did not meet these requirements. It found that Sue knew about the hospital sale, did not disclose the notice during negotiations and used it while seeking additional concessions concerning access to the ranch. It concluded that her conduct improperly contributed to PVHP abandoning the agreement.The justices also upheld the damages calculation. The proposed transactions totalled $126,000, while Chuck and Deb had retained $24,768 in non-refundable deposits. The remaining $101,232 represented the amount they lost when the sale failed. The court found that Sue had not provided evidence of the property's market value to support reducing the award. It therefore affirmed the full damages amount.The Supreme Court declined to consider her separate challenge to the order requiring her to pay for relocating the easement road because she had raised that issue for the first time on appeal. The November 20, 2026, decision ultimately upheld the district court's judgment, leaving the $101,232 award against Sue in place.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
